approach: Three changes, each where the fault starts. (1) Driver (claude.rs): split `ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke` into a private `invoke_once` and a wrapper. When the finished call is an error result whose detail is an API Error 401, the wrapper waits a short injectable time (`auth_retry_wait`, default 30 s, polled against the kill switch) and calls `invoke_once` once more, returning that second output whatever it is. The 401 test is the existing `api_error_status`, moved from disk.rs into athena-agent as a public function, so the driver and `StopCause::of` share one parser. (2) Keep-work (producer.rs, run/mod.rs): the producer-failure branch at producer.rs:384 asks `StopCause::of(&producer_stop_reason(detail))`. For `ProducerAuth` it calls `keep_unfinished_work`, the renamed and generalised `keep_timed_out_work`. That builds the candidate commit, writes progress-note.md and puts the candidate in the closing as a deadline does, but leaves the state Failed and uses the `environment: producer login expired: ...` reason plus `; its edits are kept as candidate <short>`. Every other failure, 429 included, still goes to `self.failure` and keeps nothing. (3) Resume: `timeout_seed` (mod.rs:881) accepts a Closed(TimedOut) job or a Closed(Failed) job with a login-expiry reason, through a new `disk::keeps_unfinished_work(state, reason)`. The retry then uses the existing seed path: `seed_commit`, the Resume section of the brief and the snapshot built from the candidate. No resume mark is written, because a mark makes `resume_seed` skip the producer and go to checks and the verifier, which is wrong for unfinished work. The job closes Failed with an environment reason, so `resumable_stop`, the scope guard and the drain are unchanged. Tests: fake-driver tests in run/tests.rs and cli/tests/retry.rs for the stop and the resume, stand-in-binary tests in claude.rs for the driver retry, a table test in disk.rs, and a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Reuse the deadline's keep-work function for a login expiry (renamed `keep_unfinished_work`, with a parameter for how the job ends) and extend `timeout_seed` to a Failed job with a login-expiry reason. Write no resume mark.
decisions.reason: A deadline and a login expiry both leave a partly done work tree. The timeout path already builds the candidate, progress note and brief, and a retry already resumes the producer from them (producer.rs:136, mod.rs:1162 and 1288). No resume mark means `resume_seed` stays None, so the retry runs a producer on the partial work instead of skipping to checks.

rejected.option: Write a resume mark (`write_resume_mark`) and let `resume_candidate` handle it.
rejected.why: `resume_candidate` runs no planner or producer and goes to checks and the verifier. It would verify unfinished work and never let the producer finish it.
`StopCause::of` and `resumable_stop` would no longer see an environment stop; the scope guard would count it as work and the drain would not end the batch.
It would duplicate the commit, note and redaction code and drift from the deadline path.

decisions.choice: Move `api_error_status` from disk.rs to `athena_agent::claude` (public) and import it in disk.rs. The driver's retry test is `outcome == Error && api_error_status(detail) == Some(401)`.
decisions.reason: athena-agent cannot depend on athena-core (core depends on agent). One parser means the driver retries exactly what the core classifies as a login expiry.

rejected.why: Two parsers of the same text can disagree about which forms are 401.
The brief puts the retry in claude.rs, and a retry in core would be applied to the fake driver, hiding the stop the core test must show.

decisions.choice: Only a 401 keeps work. A 429 usage limit, low disk and other errors behave as today.
decisions.reason: The request puts 429 handling out of scope and criterion 6 requires the 429 and low-disk paths to keep their behavior. `StopCause::ProducerAuth` alone selects the new branch.

rejected.option: Keep work for every environment stop (`is_environment`).
rejected.why: That changes 429 behavior, which is out of scope.

decisions.choice: The retry waits 30 seconds (constant `AUTH_RETRY_WAIT`, copied into a private field `auth_retry_wait` that tests lower to milliseconds). Only the second output is returned and recorded.
decisions.reason: The brief asks for a short wait and one retry. The field follows the existing `min_stall_window` pattern of a private field lowered in the same file's tests. A 401 call spends little, so the unrecorded first-call usage is small (an estimate).

rejected.option: Wait minutes or loop until the login returns.
rejected.why: The brief says once, after a short wait; a long wait holds a worker.

rejected.option: Add the first call's usage to the second output.
rejected.why: More driver code for a call that normally spends nothing; listed as a risk.

risks.risk: The driver's retry re-runs the whole producer conversation in the same work tree. The first call's edits are still on disk, but the model does not know it made them and may redo or contradict them.
risks.mitigation: This is what the brief asks for (retry the driver call once). The send-back, format step, checks and verifier still judge the final tree. If the retry fails too, the 401 stop keeps the tree and the note for a resume.

risks.risk: The first failed call's cost and usage are not recorded, because only the retried call's output is returned.
risks.mitigation: A 401 is returned before model work, so the loss is expected to be small (an estimate, not measured). It is a known gap; adding the first call's usage is a follow-up.

risks.risk: A 30 s wait may be shorter than the time the login takes to refresh (the incident says minutes).
risks.mitigation: The brief asks for a short wait and one retry. If the login is still expired the job stops as an environment stop with its work kept, and `athena retry` resumes it. The wait is one constant.
The wait sleeps in one-second slices and checks `registry.stopped()`, returning `DriverError::Stopped` as the start of `invoke_once` does. Tests use a 300 ms wait, so they run fast.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_producer_login_expiry_keeps_its_edits_and_closes_as_an_environment_stop` in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs. The script is `base_script()` wrapped like `timing_out()` (tests.rs:5191): for the producer it sets outcome Error, structured None and detail `crate::disk::driver_detail(&result_line("success", EXPIRED_LOGIN_TEXT))`. That is the real `output_from_result` text `success: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 ... OAuth access token has expired`. The producer still edits README.md. It runs `finished_job(&athena)` (ask, then go). Assertions: state Failed; the reason starts with `PRODUCER_AUTH`, contains `its edits are kept as candidate`, and `is_environment_reason` is true. `Records::load` gives a job candidate with a commit and `git.show_file(commit, "README.md")` equals the producer's text. `progress-note` is among the job's briefs and names README.md. `athena.state.read_resume(&id)` is None. Counts are one producer and no verifier. A second test, `a_login_expiry_with_no_edit_keeps_nothing_and_a_usage_limit_keeps_nothing`, covers a producer with no edit (the note says `Nothing was kept`, no candidate) and a 429 detail with edits (state Failed, reason starts with `USAGE_LIMIT`, `job.candidate` None).
demonstrations.observes: The tests pass: the job closes Failed with a reason starting `environment: producer login expired`, the closing record holds a candidate commit whose README.md is the producer's edit, a progress note exists, no resume mark exists and no verifier ran. The 429 case keeps no candidate.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new branch in producer.rs the 401 goes to `self.failure(...)`: the reason has no `kept as candidate` text, `job.candidate` is None and there is no progress-note, so the candidate and note assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: New test `retrying_a_login_expiry_stop_resumes_from_the_kept_work` in crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs, modelled on lifecycle.rs:3126. The script wraps `Scenario::default().script()` with a `reading(&[("README.md","modify"),("src/partial.rs","create")], ...)`. On the first producer call it returns outcome Error with the 401 detail literal (`success: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 ...`) and edits `src/partial.rs` and README.md. Later producer calls record whether `src/partial.rs` exists in the workdir and the user prompt, then finish normally. Steps: `athena.ask`, `go` (Failed, environment reason), `athena.check_history()` has no violations, `athena.retry(first)`, `go(second)`. Assertions: the second producer saw `src/partial.rs` before it did anything; its brief contains `## Resume`, the first job id and `kept as candidate <short>`; the retry lands and `fx.file("src/partial.rs")` holds the first run's content; `repo/kept/<first>` does not exist. A companion test in tests.rs, `timeout_seed_resumes_a_login_expiry_stop_but_not_other_failures`, calls `athena.timeout_seed(&records, "try again on <job>", &head)`: Some with `commit` equal to the candidate for the 401 job, None for a Failed work failure and for a 429 job.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test retry login_expiry && cargo test -p athena-core timeout_seed
demonstrations.observes: The retry's producer starts with the earlier edits in its work tree and a Resume section naming the stopped job; the retry lands with the earlier file included. `timeout_seed` returns the kept commit only for the login-expiry job.
demonstrations.fails_without: With `timeout_seed` still requiring `TimedOut`, the retry starts from the base: `src/partial.rs` is absent when the producer starts and the brief has no `## Resume`, so the retry assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_login_expiry_is_retried_once_and_a_second_call_succeeds` in the `stand_in_tests` module of crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs. The stand-in shell script gets a `MODE=auth_once` branch that counts calls in the file named by env `COUNT_FILE`. On call 1 it prints a `result` line with subtype `success`, `is_error` true and the 401 text; on later calls it prints the normal success result. The test builds the driver with the module's `driver()` helper, sets `driver.auth_retry_wait = Duration::from_millis(300)`, calls `driver.invoke(&spec(...), &mut Recorder::default())` with `COUNT_FILE` in `spec.env`, and asserts: outcome Success, `structured["answer"] == 42`, the count file reads `2`, elapsed time at least 300 ms. A second test, `a_usage_limit_is_not_retried`, uses a stand-in 429 result and asserts the count file reads `1`.
demonstrations.observes: The first call returns a 401 error result, the driver waits, the second call succeeds, and the stand-in's call count is exactly 2. The 429 result is called once.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the wrapper in `invoke`, the first call's 401 Error is returned: the outcome is Error and the count is 1, so the Success and count assertions fail.
